--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_interval_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the interval graph of a list of closed intervals. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_interval_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Add the interval graph of a list of closed intervals. title: >- [Graph.add_interval_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add the interval graph of a list of closed intervals. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add the interval graph of a list of closed intervals. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14880-L14987){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_interval_graph( intervals, interval_attr="interval", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Interval graph](/assets/graphs/add-interval-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three interval graphs, each interval drawn as a faint bar on its own row with its node at the middle. Two nodes are joined when their intervals overlap, touching endpoints included: the third interval of the first set meets neither of the others, and the long second interval of the last set overlaps three of the other four." width="100%"} Creates one node per interval `(lo, hi)`, in order, and joins two nodes when their intervals overlap, touching endpoints included (the intervals are closed). Interval graphs model anything that occupies a span of time or space: meetings that clash, genes that overlap on a chromosome, tasks that run at the same time. They are chordal and perfect, so problems that are hard in general, such as coloring (assigning rooms or registers) and maximum clique (the busiest moment), are easy on them. The edges are found by sorting the intervals and sweeping, in time proportional to `n log n` plus the number of edges. Each node's interval is stored as a `(lo, hi)` tuple in the `interval_attr=` node attribute. Unlike NetworkX's `interval_graph()`, which uses the intervals themselves as nodes, a repeated interval gets its own node (joined to its twin) rather than becoming a single node with a self-loop. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Interval graphs are useful for: - scheduling and resource allocation: overlapping bookings, register allocation, frequency assignment - genomics: overlapping reads, genes or regulatory regions - test cases for chordal and perfect graph algorithms ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [intervals]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[float, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The intervals, each a `(lo, hi)` pair of numbers (a list or tuple) with `lo <= hi`. [interval_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["interval"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's interval. Default is `"interval"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an interval is not a sequence of two values. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an interval has its lower value second or an endpoint is NaN. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four meetings, in hours. The first two touch at 10:00, so they count as overlapping: ::: {#3f13a6d7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec meetings = [(9.0, 10.0), (10.0, 11.5), (13.0, 14.0), (11.0, 13.0)] graph = ec.Graph().add_interval_graph(meetings) graph.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1--2', '2--4', '3--4'] ``` ::: ::: Each node keeps its interval: ::: {#a7eaf6be .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df().select("label", "interval", "degree") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Interval graphs are chordal, and a greedy coloring gives the number of rooms needed: ::: {#93808ddc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_chordal(), len(set(graph.greedy_color().values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, 2) ``` ::: :::
